draft.title: Vertical dilations
card: The graph of y = kf(x) is the graph of y = f(x) with every y value multiplied by k. The graph is stretched away from the x-axis, or squashed towards it, in the vertical direction.
If k is greater than 1, the graph stretches away from the x-axis. If k is between 0 and 1, it is squashed towards the x-axis. The x values do not change.
Points on the x-axis stay where they are, because 0 × k = 0. So the x-intercepts do not move. The y-intercept is multiplied by k.
Example: f(x) = x² − 4 has the point (3, 5). For y = 2f(x), the point becomes (3, 10). The x-intercepts at x = −2 and x = 2 stay the same.
draft.remember: In y = kf(x), multiply every y value by k. The x values and x-intercepts stay put.

a.q: The graph of y = f(x) passes through (4, 6). Which point must lie on y = 3f(x)?
a.why: Multiplying the y value by 3 gives 6 × 3 = 18, and x stays at 4. The point (12, 6) is tempting, but that multiplies x, which a vertical dilation does not do.
a.clue: Only the y value is multiplied by k.

b.q: The graph of y = f(x) has x-intercepts at x = 1 and x = 5, and a y-intercept at (0, 10). What are the intercepts of y = 2f(x)?
b.why: On the x-axis y = 0, and 2 × 0 = 0, so the x-intercepts stay at 1 and 5. The y-intercept is multiplied by 2, giving (0, 20). Doubling the x-intercepts is wrong, as x values do not change.
b.clue: Which values does k multiply, and what is 0 × k?

check.summary: No problems found. The example checks out, since 3² − 4 = 5 and doubling gives (3, 10), and both questions have exactly one correct option, matching the writer's explanations.
